a: ‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.

‘Anzalnahu’: We began sending down the Great Qur’an by way of revelation; or: We sent it down all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven and placed it in the House of Honour, then Jibril, peace be upon him, used to bring it down in portions over twenty years.
A preposition conveying the meaning of literal temporal containment.

‘The Night of Qadr’: the night of honour, merit, and greatness; it is called the Night of Qadr because it is the night of decreeing matters and rulings: in it Allah decrees the affairs of the year for His servants and His lands until the following year.

The angels: a kind of Allah the Exalted’s creation; they have subtle bodies of light and take whatever forms they wish; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.
